title: A passenger's iPhone Crash Detection sends a 'strong impact' alert to the local fire service before a sightseeing helicopter near Mount Aso goes missing, 20 January 2026
summary: SETN (21 Jan 2026, citing Japanese media): the helicopter took off at 10:52 on 20 Jan 2026 and lost contact at 11:04; the fire department had already received a collision notification from a passen...
account: Taiwan's SETN reported on 21 Jan 2026, citing Japanese media, that a sightseeing helicopter operated by Aso Cadre Dominion with a pilot in his sixties and two Taiwanese passengers (a 41-year-old man and a 36-year-old woman) took off at 10:52 Japan time on 20 Jan 2026 and lost contact at 11:04. Before contact was lost, the local fire department received a 'strong impact' notification from a passenger's phone, apparently the iPhone Crash Detection feature, though callbacks to the phone failed; an object believed to be the helicopter was found around the first crater of Mount Aso's Nakadake. The article does not state the fate of the three occupants, does not cite a named Japanese agency, and quotes a firefighter and a nurse on crash detection in general. Apple's feature, on iPhone 14 and later, uses motion sensors and an on-device algorithm to call emergency services after a 10-second countdown. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the case (2026-01-20-af0b) as a protective response. The link to transport safety is indirect: the device alerted responders to an aviation crash it did not prevent.
purpose: Crash Detection is built to recognize a severe vehicle crash from motion and sound signals and alert emergency services automatically.
model_version: iPhone 14或後續機型（所有機型），且搭載iOS 16
taxonomy_note: Crash notification to firefighters is read as a rescue; the occupants' outcome is not established.

ratings.reason: The fire service received an automatic impact alert before the aircraft was reported missing; the article does not quantify how it shaped the search.
The source does not state whether the occupants survived.

ai_role.statement: The phone's crash algorithm sent the notification; the search located the wreckage the following day, and the source on file does not say the alert's coordinates guided it or that anyone was rescued alive.

An impact profile that met the algorithm's severity threshold
A cellular or emergency-SOS path from a volcanic mountain area

headline: Apple Crash Detection alerts firefighters to a Mount Aso crash

later.note: The alert located the crash site but no one was rescued: on 18 February 2026 the fire department said bodies believed to be the three occupants had been found inside the crater, so the 'rapid rescue' framing of the first reports was not borne out.
later.quote: Bodies believed to be those of three people aboard a sightseeing helicopter that crashed into a volcanic crater on Mt. Aso in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, in January have been found, the local fire department said Wednesday (Feb 18).
